concepts.name: Big-O notation
concepts.gloss: A way of comparing growth rates of functions, ignoring constant factors.

concepts.name: Polynomials
concepts.gloss: Finite sums of powers of a variable with coefficients, multiplied and reduced in the usual way.

concepts.name: Complex numbers
concepts.gloss: Numbers a + bi with real a and b and imaginary unit i, with i² = −1.

concepts.name: Turing machines and tapes
concepts.gloss: A finite-state machine that reads and writes symbols on one or more tapes, each with a movable head.

concepts.name: Fixed-tape machine model
concepts.gloss: A Turing machine with one fixed finite alphabet and one fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes, whose size does not grow with the input.

evidence.quote: A machine has one fixed finite alphabet and one fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes

concepts.name: Exact integer multiplication
concepts.gloss: Given binary strings x and y of length n, output the 2n-bit binary representation of their product.

evidence.quote: We consider exact multiplication

concepts.name: The n log n optimality conjecture
concepts.gloss: The conjecture that n log n is the optimal order of growth of the time needed to multiply two n-bit integers.

evidence.quote: proposed n log n as the optimal order of growth

concepts.name: Established O(n log n) multiplier
concepts.gloss: The known fixed-tape integer multiplier running in O(n log n) time, used here only as a black-box subroutine.

evidence.quote: Calls to the established O(n log n)

concepts.name: Radix-digit convolution
concepts.gloss: Writing both integers as polynomials in a power of two whose coefficients are their digits, so that their product is a polynomial convolution of short coefficients.

evidence.quote: Splitting the inputs into radix digits reduces multiplication to convolution of short integer coefficients

concepts.name: Discrete Fourier transform
concepts.gloss: The map sending a vector of q values to its q values weighted by powers of a q-th root of unity, normalized by 1/q.

evidence.quote: We now implement the normalized Fourier transforms needed for convolution

concepts.name: Cyclic convolution
concepts.gloss: The product of two sequences in which indices wrap around modulo the sequence length.

evidence.quote: denote cyclic convolution in the displayed axes

concepts.name: Gaussian resampling
concepts.gloss: A technique that replaces a Fourier transform of arbitrary length by transforms whose axis lengths are powers of two, using Gaussian weights to move between the two sets of frequencies.

evidence.quote: it replaces the Fourier transforms needed for this convolution by multidimensional transforms whose

concepts.name: Chinese-remainder map
concepts.gloss: A relabeling of coefficient positions by mixed-radix digits for pairwise coprime lengths, which turns one cyclic convolution into a multidimensional cyclic convolution.

evidence.quote: a Chinese-remainder map that preserves convolution

concepts.name: Bluestein's chirp identity
concepts.gloss: An identity that rewrites a Fourier transform as a cyclic convolution multiplied by chirp factors, so that it can be computed with convolution.

evidence.quote: Bluestein’s chirp identity converts the middle transform

concepts.name: Synthetic polynomial transforms
concepts.gloss: Fourier-type transforms whose roots of unity are powers of y in a polynomial ring, so that multiplying by a root is a signed shift of coefficients.

evidence.quote: These are the synthetic polynomial transforms of Nussbaumer and Quandalle and

concepts.name: Polynomial ring modulo y^r + 1
concepts.title: Polynomial ring modulo $y^r + 1$

symbols.name: polynomial variable
symbols.meaning: The indeterminate of the polynomial ring, whose powers act as roots of unity.

symbols.name: record length
symbols.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in a polynomial record, a power of two.

concepts.gloss: The ring of polynomials with complex coefficients in which y^r is identified with −1, so that y has order 2r and wrap-around flips a sign.

evidence.quote: the coefficient list of a polynomial modulo y r + 1

concepts.name: Phase twist
concepts.gloss: A coefficientwise multiplication by roots of unity that converts the last cyclic coordinate into a polynomial ring, so its wrap-around becomes the negative wrap of that ring.

evidence.quote: A phase twist changes the last cyclic coordinate

concepts.name: Signed coefficient packing
concepts.gloss: Encoding polynomial coefficients, including negative ones, as one large integer by fixed-width blocks, so that polynomial multiplication becomes integer multiplication.

evidence.quote: Signed coefficient packing is a form of Kronecker substitution

concepts.name: Convolution over the polynomial ring
concepts.gloss: The normalized product of two arrays of records in the polynomial ring, computed by two forward synthetic transforms, a pointwise product, and an opposite transform.

evidence.quote: The two forward synthetic transforms retain the same frequency order

concepts.name: Subspace labels
concepts.gloss: Nondegenerate subspaces of a fixed bilinear space attached to each wire of a network, whose inclusions control how much work a change of representation costs.

evidence.quote: A label is a nondegenerate subspace of a fixed bilinear

concepts.name: Linear networks and frames
concepts.gloss: A fixed linear network that exchanges two banks of values while restoring scratch values, in which each vertex carries an invertible operator called its frame.

evidence.quote: Each procedure arises from its own fixed linear network that exchanges two banks of values

concepts.name: Subset-intersection network
concepts.gloss: A linear network on the three-element subsets of a ground set, whose wires carry scalars and whose gates combine them by intersection size, so that it swaps two banks while cancelling arbitrary scratch values.

evidence.quote: The construction uses three-element subsets: gather and scatter create coefficients

concepts.name: Address-field interchange
concepts.gloss: A tape procedure that swaps two disjoint contiguous address fields of an array in time that grows like a power of the field width, rather than linearly.

evidence.quote: The first procedure interchanges two disjoint contiguous address fields of u bits in an array

concepts.name: Address shear
concepts.gloss: The map that updates two address fields H, D to H + D, D, which is implemented by a small number of field interchanges.

evidence.quote: that endpoint operator is an address shear

concepts.name: Rank-saving recursion
concepts.gloss: The recursion in which each call splits into s smaller calls on streams of 1/W of the volume, where s < W m, so that the cost grows by the strictly smaller factor s/W per level.

evidence.quote: the total number s of smaller calls satisfies s < W m

concepts.name: Gaussian dyadics
concepts.gloss: Complex numbers whose real and imaginary parts are integers divided by a power of two, with the Gaussian integer part also an integer.

evidence.quote: Intermediate values are exact Gaussian dyadics

concepts.name: Complex phase network
concepts.gloss: A subset-intersection network whose frame change on each edge is a product of two-point kernels aI + bX on Gaussian dyadic values.

evidence.quote: The complex phase network of Proposition 8

concepts.name: Simultaneous butterfly layer
concepts.gloss: The tensor product of the two-point map H0 applied to several selected address bits at once, computed exactly in one pass rather than one axis at a time.

evidence.quote: a common butterfly layer on several axes

concepts.name: Packed selected-bit addition
concepts.gloss: An operation that adds one selected bit position across several address chunks at once, using cyclic shifts and a small deterministic correction for exceptional addresses.

evidence.quote: Packed selected-bit addition on one rectangle

concepts.name: Guard-width bound
concepts.gloss: An explicit number of extra fractional and integer bits that makes every intermediate coefficient of a butterfly layer exact, so that a single final truncation suffices.

evidence.quote: An explicit guard-width bound

concepts.name: Transform layout
concepts.gloss: A permutation of address bits that places the selected bits of all participating axes at a common offset in consecutive chunks, so that a simultaneous butterfly layer applies to each transform round.

evidence.quote: A layout on which the parallel layers apply

concepts.name: Prime source lengths
concepts.gloss: Distinct odd primes chosen close to the powers of two that are the padded axis lengths, so that their product fills a fixed fraction of the padded box.

evidence.quote: The distinct prime lengths si must be close to the powers of two ti

concepts.name: Transform identity with retained permutations
concepts.gloss: The Gaussian resampling identity in which the source and target coordinate permutations are kept as part of the formula, so that they cancel across a convolution instead of being executed as sorts.

evidence.quote: We retain both permutations in the transform formula

concepts.name: Carry propagation
concepts.gloss: Converting the recovered integer radix-digit coefficients into a binary string by adding each coefficient to a carry from the previous position.

evidence.quote: Propagate radix-2b carries in increasing coefficient order

concepts.name: Exact coefficient recovery
concepts.gloss: The error analysis showing that the computed convolution coefficients are within a half of their true integer values, so rounding recovers them exactly.

evidence.quote: proves that the recovered coefficient error is strictly below 1/2

concepts.name: Integer multiplication below n log n
concepts.gloss: A deterministic fixed-tape machine that multiplies two n-bit integers exactly in O(n (lg n)^(1−κ)) time with κ = 2^−182, which disproves the n log n optimality conjecture in this model.

evidence.quote: There is one deterministic Turing machine A

concepts.name: Axis length
concepts.gloss: The number of positions along one coordinate axis of a multidimensional array; a multidimensional transform is applied along each axis in turn, with its own length.

evidence.quote: axis lengths are powers of two

concepts.name: Coprime integers
concepts.gloss: Two integers are coprime when their greatest common divisor is 1; a family of integers is pairwise coprime when every two of them are coprime.

evidence.quote: pairwise coprime

concepts.name: Gaussian width
concepts.gloss: The integer parameter that sets how wide the Gaussian weights are in a resampling; a larger value makes the weights decay more slowly, so the resampling is more accurate.

evidence.quote: 2 ≤ α < p be integers

concepts.name: Linear map
concepts.gloss: A map between vectors of numbers that preserves addition and scalar multiplication, so that each output coordinate is a fixed weighted sum of the input coordinates.

evidence.quote: A gate is a fixed linear map on a specified set of

concepts.name: Modular arithmetic
concepts.gloss: Arithmetic in which values are reduced to their remainders on division by a fixed modulus q, so that index positions wrap around after q.

evidence.quote: All subscripts on a vector of length q are taken modulo q.

concepts.name: Operator norm
concepts.gloss: For a linear map, the largest factor by which it stretches a vector measured in a fixed norm, taken over all vectors of norm at most one.

evidence.quote: All operator norms are induced by this norm

concepts.name: Tensor product
concepts.gloss: The product of two linear maps or arrays acting on separate coordinates, so that applying the product acts on each coordinate in turn.

evidence.quote: For the tensor product, apply the one-dimensional maps to one coordinate line at a time.

concepts.name: Chinese remainder theorem
concepts.gloss: The theorem that a system of congruences with pairwise coprime moduli has a unique solution modulo the product of the moduli.

evidence.quote: Cooley used the Chinese remainder theorem to convert one cyclic convolution into multidimensional

concepts.name: Convolution theorem
concepts.gloss: The fact that the transform of a convolution of two sequences is the pointwise product of their transforms.

concepts.name: Gaussian function
concepts.gloss: The bell-shaped function x ↦ e^(−x²), or a scaled and shifted copy of it, used as a smooth weight that decays rapidly away from its centre.

concepts.name: Matrix product
concepts.gloss: The matrix whose (i, j) entry is the sum over k of the entry in row i, column k of the first matrix times the entry in row k, column j of the second; it represents the composition of the two linear maps.

concepts.name: Transform
concepts.gloss: A linear map from one array of values to another array of the same kind, each output being a fixed weighted sum of the inputs, such as a discrete Fourier transform.

It does not say that the starting point (the Harvey and van der Hoeven reduction) uses power-of-two transforms; it describes the transforms introduced in place of the starting point's Fourier transforms. The later gaussian-resampling page should use another letter for the frequency index, or say that s here is the source length and not a summation index.

$p$ means precision here, but coefficient index on [Radix-digit convolution](radix-digit-convolution.md), which this page builds on: On gaussian-resampling, p is the integer precision of the approximation; on radix-digit-convolution p is a coefficient index of c. The later gaussian-resampling page should use another letter for the precision, or say that p here is the precision, not a coefficient index.

$p$ means precision here, but output position on [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md), which this page builds on: On gaussian-resampling, p is the integer precision; on the DFT page p is an output position running over 0..q-1. The later gaussian-resampling page should use another letter for the precision, or say that p here is the precision, not an output position.
radix-digit-convolution: $a$ means digit list of x here, but input vector on [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md), which this page builds on: On radix-digit-convolution, a is the list of radix digits of x (length d, integer digits a_0..a_{d-1}); on the DFT page a is a generic vector of q complex numbers. The later page should use another letter for the digit list (for example a digit name tied to x), or say that a here is the digit list, padded to length q only when transformed.

$e$ means digit position here, but integer exponent on [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md), which this page builds on: On radix-digit-convolution, e is a digit position running over 0..d-1; on the DFT page e is an integer exponent of omega. The later radix page should use another letter for the digit position, or say that e here is a digit position, not an exponent.

$z$ means formal variable here, but integer to encode on [Exact integer multiplication](exact-integer-multiplication.md), which this page builds on: On radix-digit-convolution, z is a formal polynomial variable; on exact-integer-multiplication z is a nonnegative integer below 2^k. $c$ means convolution here, but pointwise product on [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md), which this page builds on: On radix-digit-convolution, c is the coefficient list of the product a(z)b(z), i.e. the convolution; on the DFT page c is the entrywise product of transforms. axis-length.name: first axis length
axis-length.meaning: The number of positions along the first axis of a two-dimensional array.
axis-length.quote: For a two-dimensional array with axis lengths $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$, the first axis has $\ell_1$ positions and the second has $\ell_2$.

axis-length.name: second axis length
axis-length.meaning: The number of positions along the second axis of a two-dimensional array.
axis-length.quote: For a two-dimensional array with axis lengths $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$, the first axis has $\ell_1$ positions and the second has $\ell_2$.

convolution-theorem.name: number of axes
convolution-theorem.meaning: The number of axes of an array, which counts its dimensions.
convolution-theorem.quote: Let $d$ be the number of axes of an array, let $s_i$ be the length of axis $i$, and let $S=\prod_i s_i$ be the number of positions in the array.

convolution-theorem.name: axis length
convolution-theorem.meaning: The length of axis i of the array, which counts the positions along that axis.
convolution-theorem.quote: Let $d$ be the number of axes of an array, let $s_i$ be the length of axis $i$, and let $S=\prod_i s_i$ be the number of positions in the array.

convolution-theorem.name: array size
convolution-theorem.meaning: The number of positions in the array, which is the product of the axis lengths s_i.
convolution-theorem.quote: Let $d$ be the number of axes of an array, let $s_i$ be the length of axis $i$, and let $S=\prod_i s_i$ be the number of positions in the array.

convolution-theorem.name: normalized transform
convolution-theorem.meaning: The discrete Fourier transform applied along every axis of the array, normalized by 1/S.
convolution-theorem.quote: The theorem takes its transforms by the [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) $F_s$, applied along every axis and normalized by $1/S$.

cyclic-convolution.name: cyclic convolution
cyclic-convolution.meaning: The cyclic convolution operation, which takes two vectors of q values to a vector of q values.
cyclic-convolution.quote: We write $u \ast v$ for the cyclic convolution of $u$ and $v$.

discrete-fourier-transform.name: vector length
discrete-fourier-transform.meaning: The number of values in each vector, which is the number of complex entries a transform takes.
discrete-fourier-transform.quote: Let $q$ be the number of values in each vector, and let $\omega$ be a primitive $q$-th root of unity, meaning $\omega^q=1$ and $\omega^m\neq 1$ for each integer exponent $m$ with $0<m<q$.

discrete-fourier-transform.name: root of unity
discrete-fourier-transform.meaning: A primitive $q$-th root of unity: a complex number with $\omega^q=1$ and no smaller positive power equal to 1.
discrete-fourier-transform.quote: Let $q$ be the number of values in each vector, and let $\omega$ be a primitive $q$-th root of unity, meaning $\omega^q=1$ and $\omega^m\neq 1$ for each integer exponent $m$ with $0<m<q$.

discrete-fourier-transform.name: exponent
discrete-fourier-transform.meaning: An integer exponent of omega, ranging over the values with $0<m<q$ in the primitivity condition.
discrete-fourier-transform.quote: Let $q$ be the number of values in each vector, and let $\omega$ be a primitive $q$-th root of unity, meaning $\omega^q=1$ and $\omega^m\neq 1$ for each integer exponent $m$ with $0<m<q$.

discrete-fourier-transform.name: input vector
discrete-fourier-transform.meaning: A vector of $q$ complex numbers, written $(a_0,\dots,a_{q-1})$, that the transform acts on.
discrete-fourier-transform.quote: Let $a=(a_0,\dots,a_{q-1})$ and $b$ be vectors of $q$ complex numbers, with input positions $j$ and output positions $p$ running from $0$ to $q-1$.

discrete-fourier-transform.name: second vector
discrete-fourier-transform.meaning: A second vector of $q$ complex numbers, used with $a$ in the convolution.
discrete-fourier-transform.quote: Let $a=(a_0,\dots,a_{q-1})$ and $b$ be vectors of $q$ complex numbers, with input positions $j$ and output positions $p$ running from $0$ to $q-1$.

discrete-fourier-transform.name: input position
discrete-fourier-transform.meaning: An input position of a vector, running from $0$ to $q-1$.
discrete-fourier-transform.quote: Let $a=(a_0,\dots,a_{q-1})$ and $b$ be vectors of $q$ complex numbers, with input positions $j$ and output positions $p$ running from $0$ to $q-1$.

discrete-fourier-transform.name: output position
discrete-fourier-transform.meaning: An output position of a transformed vector, running from $0$ to $q-1$.
discrete-fourier-transform.quote: Let $a=(a_0,\dots,a_{q-1})$ and $b$ be vectors of $q$ complex numbers, with input positions $j$ and output positions $p$ running from $0$ to $q-1$.

discrete-fourier-transform.name: transform map
discrete-fourier-transform.meaning: The discrete Fourier transform on vectors of length $q$, whose entries are the weighted sums $(F_q a)_p$.
discrete-fourier-transform.quote: The transform $F_q$ sends $a$ to the vector with entries

discrete-fourier-transform.name: opposite transform
discrete-fourier-transform.meaning: The transform on vectors of length $q$ defined like $F_q$ but with $\omega^{-1}$ in place of $\omega$.
discrete-fourier-transform.quote: and the opposite transform $F_q^+$ uses $\omega^{-1}$ in place of $\omega$.

discrete-fourier-transform.name: frequency index
discrete-fourier-transform.meaning: The summation index over frequencies, running from $0$ to $q-1$.
discrete-fourier-transform.quote: For an integer exponent $e$, the sum $\sum_{s=0}^{q-1}\omega^{es}$ over the frequency index $s$ equals $q$ if $q$ divides $e$, and $0$ otherwise.

discrete-fourier-transform.name: integer exponent
discrete-fourier-transform.meaning: An integer exponent of omega in the full-period sum.
discrete-fourier-transform.quote: For an integer exponent $e$, the sum $\sum_{s=0}^{q-1}\omega^{es}$ over the frequency index $s$ equals $q$ if $q$ divides $e$, and $0$ otherwise.

discrete-fourier-transform.name: pointwise product
discrete-fourier-transform.meaning: The entrywise product of the transforms of $a$ and $b$.
discrete-fourier-transform.quote: Let $c=(F_qa)\cdot(F_qb)$ be the entrywise product, and write $h$ for an input position of $b$.

discrete-fourier-transform.name: input position of b
discrete-fourier-transform.meaning: An input position of the vector $b$, running from $0$ to $q-1$.
discrete-fourier-transform.quote: Let $c=(F_qa)\cdot(F_qb)$ be the entrywise product, and write $h$ for an input position of $b$.

exact-integer-multiplication.name: input length
exact-integer-multiplication.meaning: The number of bits in each of the two binary inputs.
exact-integer-multiplication.quote: Let $n$ be the number of bits in each input.

exact-integer-multiplication.name: first input
exact-integer-multiplication.meaning: The first binary string of the input, of length n.
exact-integer-multiplication.quote: Let $x$ be the first binary string, of length $n$.

exact-integer-multiplication.name: second input
exact-integer-multiplication.meaning: The second binary string of the input, also of length n.
exact-integer-multiplication.quote: Let $y$ be the second binary string, also of length $n$.

exact-integer-multiplication.name: binary value
exact-integer-multiplication.meaning: The nonnegative integer value of the binary string x, with the leftmost bit most significant.
exact-integer-multiplication.quote: For a binary string $x$ of length $n$, let $\mathrm{val}(x)$ be its nonnegative integer value, with the leftmost bit most significant.

exact-integer-multiplication.name: padded length
exact-integer-multiplication.meaning: The number of bits in a padded binary representation.
exact-integer-multiplication.quote: Let $k$ be a length in bits.

exact-integer-multiplication.name: integer to encode
exact-integer-multiplication.meaning: A nonnegative integer below 2^k that is written in binary.

exact-integer-multiplication.name: padded binary representation
exact-integer-multiplication.meaning: The binary representation of z, padded on the left with zeros to length k.
exact-integer-multiplication.quote: Let $z$ be a nonnegative integer below $2^k$, and let $\mathrm{bin}_k(z)$ be the binary representation of $z$, padded on the left with zeros to length $k$.

gaussian-function.name: evaluation point
gaussian-function.meaning: A real number at which the Gaussian function is evaluated, namely the distance from its centre.
gaussian-function.quote: Here $z$ is a real number, the distance from the centre at which the weight is evaluated.

gaussian-function.name: width parameter
gaussian-function.meaning: An integer, at least 2, that sets how wide the Gaussian bell is.
gaussian-function.quote: Here $\alpha$ is an integer width parameter with $\alpha\ge 2$, and a larger $\alpha$ gives a wider bell.

gaussian-function.name: Gaussian weight
gaussian-function.meaning: The Gaussian function $G_\alpha(z)=e^{-\pi z^2/\alpha^2}$, a bell-shaped weight centred at zero.
gaussian-function.quote: Write $G_\alpha$ for the Gaussian function, $G_\alpha(z)=e^{-\pi z^2/\alpha^2}$.

gaussian-function.name: input length

gaussian-function.quote: Let $s$ and $t$ be integers, and let $u$ be a vector of $s$ values.

gaussian-function.name: output length
gaussian-function.meaning: The number of output values, indexed from 0 to t-1, that the weighted map returns.
gaussian-function.quote: Let $s$ and $t$ be integers, and let $u$ be a vector of $s$ values.

gaussian-function.name: output position
gaussian-function.meaning: The position of an output value of the weighted map, running from 0 to t-1.
gaussian-function.quote: Here $\kappa$ is the position of an output value, and $\ell$ is a summation index over the integers.

gaussian-function.name: summation index
gaussian-function.meaning: An integer index over which the weighted sum runs.
gaussian-function.quote: Here $\kappa$ is the position of an output value, and $\ell$ is a summation index over the integers.

gaussian-function.name: Gaussian map
gaussian-function.meaning: The linear map from vectors of s values to vectors of t values whose weights are Gaussians.
gaussian-function.quote: The Gaussian function is used to build the [linear map](linear-map.md) $S$ below.

gaussian-function.name: second Gaussian map
gaussian-function.meaning: The second Gaussian-weighted map, built like S with the roles of the two grids exchanged.
gaussian-function.quote: The second map $T$ is built the same way with the roles of the two grids exchanged.

gaussian-function.name: correction map
gaussian-function.meaning: A map built from S, T, a diagonal rescaling and a coordinate selection, which is close to the identity.
gaussian-function.quote: Here $N$ is a correction map built from $S$, $T$, a diagonal rescaling and a selection of coordinates.

gaussian-function.name: length gap
gaussian-function.meaning: The relative gap t/s - 1 between the two lengths.
gaussian-function.quote: The terms of $N$ other than the selected one are negligible when $\alpha^2\theta>1$, where $\theta=t/s-1$.

gaussian-resampling.name: source length
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The number of coordinates of the source vector, the length of the transform on the source grid.
gaussian-resampling.quote: The identity is restricted to [coprime integers](coprime-integers.md) $s<t$, where $s$ is the number of coordinates of the source vector and $t$ the number of coordinates of the target.

gaussian-resampling.name: target length
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The number of coordinates of the target vector, the length of the transform on the target grid.
gaussian-resampling.quote: The identity is restricted to [coprime integers](coprime-integers.md) $s<t$, where $s$ is the number of coordinates of the source vector and $t$ the number of coordinates of the target.

gaussian-resampling.name: relative excess
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The ratio t/s minus one, measuring how much longer the target is than the source.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Let $\theta=t/s-1$ be the relative excess of $t$ over $s$.

gaussian-resampling.name: Gaussian width
gaussian-resampling.meaning: An integer, at least 2, that sets the width parameter of the Gaussian weights.
gaussian-resampling.quote: The identity needs $\theta>p/\alpha^4$, where $\alpha\ge 2$ is an integer Gaussian width and $p$ is the integer precision of the numerical approximation.

gaussian-resampling.name: precision
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The integer precision of the numerical approximation, which bounds how large theta must be.
gaussian-resampling.quote: The identity needs $\theta>p/\alpha^4$, where $\alpha\ge 2$ is an integer Gaussian width and $p$ is the integer precision of the numerical approximation.

gaussian-resampling.name: source permutation
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The permutation of length-s vectors sending u to the vector with entries u_{tj} at index j, indices taken modulo s.
gaussian-resampling.quote: The permutations $P_s$ and $P_t$ are defined using [modular arithmetic](modular-arithmetic.md) on their indices, with subscripts taken modulo the length:

gaussian-resampling.name: target permutation
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The permutation of length-t vectors sending v to the vector with entries v_{-sk} at index k, indices taken modulo t.
gaussian-resampling.quote: The permutations $P_s$ and $P_t$ are defined using [modular arithmetic](modular-arithmetic.md) on their indices, with subscripts taken modulo the length:

gaussian-resampling.name: source transform
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The normalized transform of length s, the transform F_q with q equal to s.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Write $F_s$ and $F_t$ for the normalized transforms of length $s$ and $t$, that is, $F_q$ with $q=s$ or $q=t$.

gaussian-resampling.name: target transform
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The normalized transform of length t, the transform F_q with q equal to t.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Write $F_s$ and $F_t$ for the normalized transforms of length $s$ and $t$, that is, $F_q$ with $q=s$ or $q=t$.

gaussian-resampling.name: source-to-target Gaussian map
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The Gaussian map sending length-s vectors to length-t vectors, with entries (Su)_k given by a Gaussian-weighted sum over j.
gaussian-resampling.quote: The two Gaussian maps $S$ and $T$ are built from the [Gaussian function](gaussian-function.md).

gaussian-resampling.name: target-to-source Gaussian map
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The Gaussian map sending length-s vectors to length-t vectors, with entries (Tu)_k given by a second Gaussian-weighted sum over j.
gaussian-resampling.quote: The two Gaussian maps $S$ and $T$ are built from the [Gaussian function](gaussian-function.md).

gaussian-resampling.name: nearest target index
gaussian-resampling.meaning: For each source position j, the integer nearest to tj/s, which is the target entry that C selects.
gaussian-resampling.quote: $C$ maps length-$t$ vectors to length-$s$ vectors by taking, for each $j$ with $0\le j<s$, the entry at $\mu_j$, the integer nearest to $tj/s$.

gaussian-resampling.name: selection map
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The map from length-t vectors to length-s vectors that copies the entries at the indices mu_j.
gaussian-resampling.quote: $C$ maps length-$t$ vectors to length-$s$ vectors by taking, for each $j$ with $0\le j<s$, the entry at $\mu_j$, the integer nearest to $tj/s$.

gaussian-resampling.name: diagonal correction
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The diagonal map on length-s vectors whose j-th factor cancels the Gaussian factor of T at entry mu_j.
gaussian-resampling.quote: The diagonal map $D$ is $(Du)_j=e^{\pi\alpha^2(tj/s-\mu_j)^2}u_j$ on length-$s$ vectors, which cancels the Gaussian factor of $T$ at that entry.

gaussian-resampling.name: correction map
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The map CTD on length-s vectors, which is close to the identity.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Put $N=CTD$.

gaussian-resampling.name: identity map
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The map that leaves every vector unchanged.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Its $j$th entry is $u_j$ plus other terms, so $N$ is close to $I$, the identity map, which leaves every vector unchanged.

gaussian-resampling.name: series index
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The summation index of the Neumann series, a non-negative integer.
gaussian-resampling.quote:
Here $
u$ is the summation index, and its $
u$th term has norm at most $2^{-
u}$, so the series converges.

gaussian-resampling.name: scaled diagonal map
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The diagonal map D multiplied by the scalar 2 to the power minus (2 alpha squared minus 2).
gaussian-resampling.quote: Write $D'=2^{-(2\alpha^2-2)}D$ for the scaled diagonal map.

gaussian-resampling.name: source-to-target contraction
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The contraction S/2, mapping length-s vectors to length-t vectors.
gaussian-resampling.quote: $A$ maps length-$s$ vectors to length-$t$ vectors, and $B_0$ maps them back, where $A=S/2$ and $B_0=D'N^{-1}C/2$.

gaussian-resampling.name: target-to-source contraction
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The contraction D' N^{-1} C / 2, mapping length-t vectors back to length-s vectors.
gaussian-resampling.quote: $A$ maps length-$s$ vectors to length-$t$ vectors, and $B_0$ maps them back, where $A=S/2$ and $B_0=D'N^{-1}C/2$.

linear-map.name: linear map
linear-map.meaning: The rule that takes an input vector $u$ of $m$ complex numbers and returns an output vector $v$ of $k$ complex numbers.
linear-map.quote: A linear map is a rule $L$ with two fixed sizes: $m$, the number of input coordinates, and $k$, the number of output coordinates.

linear-map.name: input vector
linear-map.meaning: The vector of $m$ complex numbers that the linear map $L$ takes as input.
linear-map.quote: It takes a vector $u$ of $m$ complex numbers and returns a vector $v$ of $k$ complex numbers, written $L:\mathbb{C}^m\to\mathbb{C}^k$.

linear-map.name: output vector
linear-map.meaning: The vector of $k$ complex numbers that the linear map $L$ returns.
linear-map.quote: It takes a vector $u$ of $m$ complex numbers and returns a vector $v$ of $k$ complex numbers, written $L:\mathbb{C}^m\to\mathbb{C}^k$.

linear-map.name: input count
linear-map.meaning: The number of input coordinates of $L$.
linear-map.quote: A linear map is a rule $L$ with two fixed sizes: $m$, the number of input coordinates, and $k$, the number of output coordinates.

linear-map.name: output count
linear-map.meaning: The number of output coordinates of $L$.
linear-map.quote: A linear map is a rule $L$ with two fixed sizes: $m$, the number of input coordinates, and $k$, the number of output coordinates.

linear-map.name: input coordinate
linear-map.meaning: The $j$-th coordinate of the input vector $u$.
linear-map.quote: Write $u_j$ for the $j$-th input coordinate of $u$, $v_i$ for the $i$-th output coordinate of $v$, and $a_{ij}$ for the weight that output $i$ gives to input $j$.

linear-map.name: output coordinate
linear-map.meaning: The $i$-th coordinate of the output vector $v$.
linear-map.quote: Write $u_j$ for the $j$-th input coordinate of $u$, $v_i$ for the $i$-th output coordinate of $v$, and $a_{ij}$ for the weight that output $i$ gives to input $j$.

linear-map.name: weight
linear-map.meaning: The fixed number by which output coordinate $i$ multiplies input coordinate $j$.
linear-map.quote: Write $u_j$ for the $j$-th input coordinate of $u$, $v_i$ for the $i$-th output coordinate of $v$, and $a_{ij}$ for the weight that output $i$ gives to input $j$.

operator-norm.name: vector norm
operator-norm.meaning: The largest modulus among the coordinates of the vector u.
operator-norm.quote: The norm of $u$, written $\|u\|$, is the largest modulus (absolute value) among its coordinates.

operator-norm.name: operator norm
operator-norm.meaning: The largest factor by which L stretches a vector of norm at most one.
operator-norm.quote: Here $\sup$ denotes the supremum, the least upper bound, so the operator norm $\|L\|$ is the least upper bound of $\|Lu\|$ over all vectors $u$ with $\|u\|\le 1$

operator-norm.name: second map
operator-norm.meaning: A second linear map whose output length matches the input length of L.
operator-norm.quote: Let $M$ be a second linear map whose output length matches the input length of $L$, so that $LM$ is defined.

operator-norm.name: contraction A
operator-norm.meaning: A linear map that is a contraction, used as a factor on the Gaussian resampling page.
operator-norm.quote: On the [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md) page, the factors $A$ and $B_0$ are linear maps that are contractions, so they cannot increase the norm of what they are applied to.

operator-norm.name: contraction B_0
operator-norm.meaning: A linear map that is a contraction, used as a factor on the Gaussian resampling page.
operator-norm.quote: On the [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md) page, the factors $A$ and $B_0$ are linear maps that are contractions, so they cannot increase the norm of what they are applied to.

radix-digit-convolution.name: radix
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: The base in which the integers are written, equal to $2^w$.
radix-digit-convolution.quote: Let $B = 2^w$ be the radix, the base in which the integers are written, with $w$ the number of bits in each radix digit.

radix-digit-convolution.name: bits per digit
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: The number of bits in each radix digit.
radix-digit-convolution.quote: Let $B = 2^w$ be the radix, the base in which the integers are written, with $w$ the number of bits in each radix digit.

radix-digit-convolution.name: digit count
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: The number of radix digits of each input.
radix-digit-convolution.quote: Let $d$ be the number of radix digits of each input, and let $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{d-1})$ be the list of digits of $x$, so $x = \sum_{e=0}^{d-1} a_e B^e$ with $0 \le a_e < B$.

radix-digit-convolution.name: digit list of x
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: The list of radix digits of the first input x, indexed from $a_0$ to $a_{d-1}$.
radix-digit-convolution.quote: Let $d$ be the number of radix digits of each input, and let $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{d-1})$ be the list of digits of $x$, so $x = \sum_{e=0}^{d-1} a_e B^e$ with $0 \le a_e < B$.

radix-digit-convolution.name: digit position
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: The position of a digit in the digit list of an input, running from $0$ to $d-1$.

radix-digit-convolution.name: digit position
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: The position of a digit in the digit list of the second input, running from $0$ to $d-1$.

radix-digit-convolution.name: formal variable
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: A placeholder for the powers of a polynomial.
radix-digit-convolution.quote: Let $z$ be a formal variable, a placeholder for the powers of a polynomial, so that $a(B) = x$ for $a(z) = \sum_e a_e z^e$.

radix-digit-convolution.name: digit list of y
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: The list of radix digits of the second input y, indexed like $a$.
radix-digit-convolution.quote: The input $y$ has digit list $b$ in the same way.

radix-digit-convolution.name: convolution
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: The list of coefficients of the product $a(z)b(z)$, which is the convolution of $a$ and $b$.
radix-digit-convolution.quote: The convolution $c = a * b$ is the list of coefficients of the product $a(z)b(z)$.

radix-digit-convolution.name: coefficient index
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: The index of a coefficient of $c$.
radix-digit-convolution.quote: Here $p$ is the index of a coefficient of $c$, so $c_p = \sum_{e+f=p} a_e b_f$.

tensor-product.name: first map
tensor-product.meaning: A linear map on vectors of length $s$.
tensor-product.quote: Let $L$ be a linear map on vectors of length $s$ and $M$ a linear map on vectors of length $t$, with entries $L_{ih}$ (row $i$, column $h$) and $M_{mg}$ (row $m$, column $g$).

tensor-product.name: second map
tensor-product.meaning: A linear map on vectors of length $t$.
tensor-product.quote: Let $L$ be a linear map on vectors of length $s$ and $M$ a linear map on vectors of length $t$, with entries $L_{ih}$ (row $i$, column $h$) and $M_{mg}$ (row $m$, column $g$).

tensor-product.name: tensor product
tensor-product.meaning: The operator that combines $L$ and $M$ into a linear map on arrays with $s$ rows and $t$ columns.
tensor-product.quote: The tensor product $L\otimes M$ is the linear map on arrays $u$ with $s$ rows and $t$ columns, entries $u_{hg}$, whose entry at position $(i,m)$ is

tensor-product.name: array
tensor-product.meaning: An array with $s$ rows and $t$ columns, whose entries are $u_{hg}$.
tensor-product.quote: The tensor product $L\otimes M$ is the linear map on arrays $u$ with $s$ rows and $t$ columns, entries $u_{hg}$, whose entry at position $(i,m)$ is

tensor-product.name: output row index
tensor-product.meaning: The index of an output row, which is the first coordinate of an output position.
tensor-product.quote: Here $i$ and $m$ index the output row and column, and $h$ and $g$ index the input row and column.

tensor-product.name: output column index
tensor-product.meaning: The index of an output column, which is the second coordinate of an output position.
tensor-product.quote: Here $i$ and $m$ index the output row and column, and $h$ and $g$ index the input row and column.

tensor-product.name: input row index
tensor-product.meaning: The index of an input row of the array $u$.
tensor-product.quote: Here $i$ and $m$ index the output row and column, and $h$ and $g$ index the input row and column.

tensor-product.name: input column index
tensor-product.meaning: The index of an input column of the array $u$.
tensor-product.quote: Here $i$ and $m$ index the output row and column, and $h$ and $g$ index the input row and column.

transform-identity.name: source transform
transform-identity.meaning: The normalized transform $F_q$ with $q=s$, acting on vectors of $s$ coordinates.
transform-identity.quote: Write $F_s$ and $F_t$ for $F_q$ with $q=s$ and $q=t$, the normalized transforms of vectors of $s$ and $t$ coordinates, and $F_s^+$ for the opposite transform $F_q^+$ with $q=s$.

transform-identity.name: target transform
transform-identity.meaning: The normalized transform $F_q$ with $q=t$, acting on vectors of $t$ coordinates.
transform-identity.quote: Write $F_s$ and $F_t$ for $F_q$ with $q=s$ and $q=t$, the normalized transforms of vectors of $s$ and $t$ coordinates, and $F_s^+$ for the opposite transform $F_q^+$ with $q=s$.

transform-identity.name: opposite source transform
transform-identity.meaning: The opposite transform $F_q^+$ with $q=s$, which uses $\omega^{-1}$ in place of $\omega$.
transform-identity.quote: Write $F_s$ and $F_t$ for $F_q$ with $q=s$ and $q=t$, the normalized transforms of vectors of $s$ and $t$ coordinates, and $F_s^+$ for the opposite transform $F_q^+$ with $q=s$.

transform-identity.name: coordinate count
transform-identity.meaning: The number of coordinates of the grid, a count.
transform-identity.quote: Here $d$ is the number of coordinates, not the digit count.

transform-identity.name: source axis length
transform-identity.meaning: The number of entries along coordinate $i$ of the source grid, a count.
transform-identity.quote: Here $s_i$ and $t_i$ are the numbers of entries along coordinate $i$ of the source and target grids.

transform-identity.name: target axis length
transform-identity.meaning: The number of entries along coordinate $i$ of the target grid, a count.
transform-identity.quote: Here $s_i$ and $t_i$ are the numbers of entries along coordinate $i$ of the source and target grids.

transform-identity.name: source permutation
transform-identity.meaning: The tensor product of the one-dimensional source permutations $P_{s_i}$, permuting the source coordinates.
transform-identity.quote: Here $R=\bigotimes_i P_{s_i}$ permutes the source coordinates, and $Q=\bigotimes_i P_{t_i}$ permutes the target coordinates.

transform-identity.name: target permutation
transform-identity.meaning: The tensor product of the one-dimensional target permutations $P_{t_i}$, permuting the target coordinates.
transform-identity.quote: Here $R=\bigotimes_i P_{s_i}$ permutes the source coordinates, and $Q=\bigotimes_i P_{t_i}$ permutes the target coordinates.

transform-identity.name: index permutation
transform-identity.meaning: The permutation $(R_c z)_j=z_{cj}$ of length-$q$ vectors, for a unit $c$ modulo $q$.
transform-identity.quote: Write $R_c$ for the permutation $(R_c z)_j=z_{cj}$ of length-$q$ vectors, where $c$ is a unit modulo $q$.

transform-identity.name: source-to-target contraction
transform-identity.meaning: The tensor product of the one-dimensional contractions $A$, mapping source arrays to target arrays.
transform-identity.quote: The letters $A$ and $B_0$ denote the one-dimensional contractions below, and after lifting they denote tensor products.

transform-identity.name: target-to-source contraction
transform-identity.meaning: The tensor product of the one-dimensional contractions $B_0$, mapping target arrays to source arrays.
transform-identity.quote: The letters $A$ and $B_0$ denote the one-dimensional contractions below, and after lifting they denote tensor products.

transform-identity.name: source array
transform-identity.meaning: An array on the source grid of shape $s_1\times\cdots\times s_d$.
transform-identity.quote: The arrays $u$ and $v$ now live on the source grid of shape $s_1\times\cdots\times s_d$.

transform-identity.name: second source array
transform-identity.meaning: A second array on the source grid of shape $s_1\times\cdots\times s_d$.
transform-identity.quote: The arrays $u$ and $v$ now live on the source grid of shape $s_1\times\cdots\times s_d$.

transform-identity.name: cyclic convolution
transform-identity.meaning: The cyclic convolution of two arrays on the source grid.
transform-identity.quote: Writing $u*v$ for the cyclic convolution on the source grid.

transform-identity.name: coordinatewise product
transform-identity.meaning: The product of two arrays taken entry by entry on the same grid.
transform-identity.quote: Permutations commute with coordinatewise products, so $(RF_su)\cdot(RF_sv)=R\big((F_su)\cdot(F_sv)\big)$, where $\cdot$ is the coordinatewise product.

axis-length.quote: An axis length is the number of positions along one coordinate axis of a multidimensional array, and it sets the length of the [Transform](transform.md) applied along that axis.
Each axis length is one factor in the [Tensor product](tensor-product.md) that gives the full transform.

convolution-theorem.quote: The theorem takes its transforms by the [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) $F_s$, applied along every axis and normalized by $1/S$.
The theorem concerns the [Cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md) $u*v$, taken along every axis, so each index wraps around modulo its axis length.

coprime-integers.quote: Coprime integers enable the splitting of one [cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md) into a multidimensional one over the same lengths.

discrete-fourier-transform.quote: The discrete Fourier transform is built as a [Linear map](linear-map.md) that sends a vector of complex numbers to another vector of the same length.

gaussian-resampling.quote: Gaussian resampling is an identity that replaces the [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) of an arbitrary length by transforms whose lengths are powers of two.
It serves the [Radix-digit convolution](radix-digit-convolution.md) of digit vectors, which needs such transforms.
The identity is restricted to [coprime integers](coprime-integers.md) $s<t$, where $s$ is the number of coordinates of the source vector and $t$ the number of coordinates of the target.
The permutations $P_s$ and $P_t$ are defined using [modular arithmetic](modular-arithmetic.md) on their indices, with subscripts taken modulo the length:
The size of $N-I$ is measured by its [operator norm](operator-norm.md), $\|N-I\|$.
The two Gaussian maps $S$ and $T$ are built from the [Gaussian function](gaussian-function.md).

operator-norm.quote: The operator norm is defined for any [linear map](linear-map.md) $L$, and it is the largest factor by which $L$ stretches a vector.

radix-digit-convolution.quote: Radix-digit convolution reduces [exact integer multiplication](exact-integer-multiplication.md) to a polynomial product whose coefficients are short integers.
Radix-digit convolution is computed by [Fourier transforms](discrete-fourier-transform.md) of length $q \ge 2d-1$.
After [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md), the convolution is computed with transforms of [axis lengths](axis-length.md) that are powers of two.

tensor-product.quote: A tensor product is built from one [Linear map](linear-map.md) for each coordinate, and it lets a map on a multidimensional array act on each coordinate in turn.

transform.quote: A transform is a [Linear map](linear-map.md) from one array of values to another array of the same kind, each output being a fixed weighted sum of the inputs.

transform-identity.quote: The one-dimensional identity is derived from [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md).
The one-dimensional identity holds for [coprime](coprime-integers.md) $s<t$ with $\theta=t/s-1$ large enough: $P_sF_s=2^{2\alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA$, with contractions $A$ and $B_0$.
The identity is lifted by a [tensor product](tensor-product.md) of the one-dimensional identities to $d$ coordinates.
The cancellation is based on the [convolution theorem](convolution-theorem.md): with the $1/q$ factor of $F_q$, $F_s(u*v)=\left(\prod_i s_i\right)(F_su)\cdot(F_sv)$.
